18. We feel lighter while floating on water. Why?
Ans:- We feel lighter while floating on water because of the upthrust (buoyant force) exerted by the water. This upward force
partially supports our weight, reducing the net force we feel on our body, making us feel lighter than on land.
19. On lifting a mug submerged in water in a bucket, it feels heaver when it comes out of the water. Why?
Ans:- When a mug is submerged in water, it experiences upthrust (buoyant force) which partially supports its weight, making
it feel lighter. When the mug is lifted out of the water, the upthrust disappears, so we feel the full weight of the mug, making
it seem heavier.
20. It is easier to float in the Dead Sea than in a swimming pool. (the density of water in the Dead Sea is 1240 kg/m³). Why?
Ans:- It is easier to float in the Dead Sea than in a swimming pool because the density of Dead Sea water (1240 kg/m³) is
much higher than that of ordinary water (≈1000 kg/m³). A higher density increases the buoyant force on the body, so the
body floats more easily and feels lighter in the Dead Sea.
21. If more passengers climb a boat than its maximum capacity, the boat is likely to sink. Why?
Ans:- If more passengers climb a boat than its maximum capacity, the total weight of the boat exceeds the buoyant force
provided by the water. According to Archimedes’ principle, a floating object displaces water equal to its weight. When the
weight is too much, the boat cannot displace enough water to stay afloat and is likely to sink.
22. Write any two applications of Pascal's law in daily life.
Ans:- Two daily applications of Pascal’s law are:
1. Hydraulic Lift: Used in garages to lift heavy vehicles by applying a small force.
2. Hydraulic Brakes: Used in vehicles to transmit force from the brake pedal to the brake pads efficiently.
23. Explain, with a figure, the cause of the production of upthrust when an object is placed on liquid.
Ans:- When an object is placed in a liquid, the pressure exerted by the liquid is greater at the bottom than at the
top because pressure increases with depth. This difference in pressure creates a net upward force on the object,
known as upthrust or buoyant force.
24. When a stone is dropped into the water, it sinks. Does this happen because of the absence of upthrust? Write with logic.
Ans:- A stone sinks in water not because upthrust is absent, but because the upward buoyant force is smaller than the weight
of the stone. First, upthrust exists for all submerged objects, including stones, and is equal to the weight of the water
displaced by the stone. Second, a stone is much denser than water, so its weight is greater than the upthrust acting on it. As a
result, the net force on the stone is downward, causing it to sink.
25. Two balloons, one filled with air and the other with hydrogen, look identical. What difference can be noticed when they
are released into the air? Explain with reasons.
Ans:- When two identical-looking balloons, one filled with air and the other with hydrogen, are released, the hydrogen-filled
balloon rises, while the air-filled balloon stays near the ground. This happens because hydrogen is much lighter than air,
making the overall density of the balloon less than the surrounding air, so the upward buoyant force exceeds its weight. In
contrast, the air-filled balloon has almost the same density as the surrounding air, so the buoyant force is nearly equal to its
weight, and it does not rise.
26. An object is suspending /floating just below the surface of the water. If the amount of salt dissolving in the water goes on
increasing, what change will occur in the position of the balloon? Explain with reasons.
Ans:- If an object is floating just below the surface of water and the amount of salt in the water is gradually increased, the
object will rise higher and may even float on the surface. This occurs because dissolving salt increases the density of the
water, and according to Archimedes’ principle, the buoyant force on an object depends on the density of the liquid. As the
water becomes denser, the buoyant force increases, providing a greater upward push on the object, which causes it to rise.
Thus, the object moves higher in the water as the salt concentration increases.
27. “Substance with a density greater than the density of the liquid sink in it." Is this statement always true? Justify with an
example.
Ans:- The statement “A substance with a density greater than the density of the liquid sinks in it” is not always true.
Justification:
 Whether an object sinks or floats depends not only on density but also on shape and volume.
